note: Adaptations of published benchmarks on one real matter. Not official leaderboard numbers. Reproduce: bun run job scripts/eval.ts --suites <ids>; bun run job scripts/eval.ts --merge

suites.name: Atomic finding recall (omission rate)
suites.origin: FActScore (Min et al., 2023, arXiv:2305.14251): atomic-fact decomposition, here used for recall instead of precision
suites.adaptation: 48 atomic findings hand-written from the independent answer key; an LLM judge (gpt-5.4-mini) checks each against gist's verified facts (top-8 hybrid hits over fact chunks), the digest, contradictions and gate items.

tables.title: Misses (omissions)
rows: Defendant bodily injury limits $100,000 / $300,000, confirmed in writing 2026-09-08

The digest states the defendant liability limits are $100,000 / $300,000 in `coverage_limit` and `coverage_lines`, but it does not state that these limits were confirmed in writing on 2026-09-08. The only 2026-09-08 item in `coverage_notes` says no excess or umbrella coverage was disclosed, which is a different point.
Firm's own case expenses (records, court filing, IME observer) have not been reimbursed

The digest JSON only lists the firm spend items and total in `money.firm_spend` (expense refs for records reproduction, IME observer, and court filing), but it does not state the core finding that these firm expenses have not been reimbursed. The unreimbursed language appears only in the retrieved verified facts for the records expenses, not in the digest/story output itself.
Metro-North incident report in defendants' discovery response marks Ferrara On-Duty, heading to the jobsite

The output matches only part of the expected finding. It confirms the incident report was in the discovery response and says Ferrara was heading to the jobsite, but it does not state the key “On-Duty” designation. Partial mention without the core point is insufficient.
Kyle Pullano was Ferrara's passenger (a witness)
The output identifies Pullano as a passenger and a witness, but not as Ferrara’s passenger. The core relationship in the expected finding is missing, so this is not a match.
Defense orthopedic IME (Hostin) finds injuries resolved and client able to return to work without restrictions

The retrieved facts include Hostin’s orthopaedic IME report and a separate Tsao opinion that the claimant can work without restrictions, but no surfaced field attributes that conclusion to Hostin. The digest’s IME gate item likewise only confirms the Hostin report was annexed/served, not its substantive conclusion.
Defense radiology review (Katzman) finds brain/DTI normal and no recent trauma in knees and right shoulder

The output only clearly states Katzman found no recent traumatic injury in the right shoulder and right knee. It does not expressly state the expected brain/DTI finding, so the full expected finding is not surfaced.
Overdue task: client's updated employment and commission records (due 2026-09-26)

The output does mention updated employment and commission records in the wage-loss documentation item (e.g., source_ref email:5029636493 and note:2997038798), but it does not state the specific overdue task with due date 2026-09-26. No field in the provided digest excerpt matches that exact task/due date.
2026 compliance conference not yet set / not calendared
The output does not state that a 2026 compliance conference was not yet set or not calendared; it says the opposite, that a further compliance conference was scheduled.
IME dates in Clio (Sept 2026) conflict with the dates in the IME reports (March 2026)

The output does state the IME reports are dated March 31, 2026 and March 24, 2026 in the phase-gate item "Defense IME reports received, with rebuttal" (doc:21122792168#p1 and doc:21122791073#p47), but it does not say those dates conflict with September 2026 Clio dates. I did not find any field or digest text explicitly noting a Clio-vs-report date conflict.
Client claims total disability while defense IME says he can return to work

The output clearly supports the first half of the finding that the client claims total disability (e.g., verified facts say he was “totally disabled from his usual occupation” and “totally disabled and incapacitated from his employment”), but it does not state the defense IME says he can return to work. The IME-related entries only say the reports are in the record or that they may be unhelpful; no cited field or fact says he can return to work.
Plaintiff's discovery response cites a different index number (150940/2024) than the caption (160000/2024)

The output contains the two index numbers separately, but it does not expressly make the comparison that the discovery response cites 150940/2024 while the caption uses 160000/2024. A partial mention of both numbers is not enough.

suites.name: Citation precision
suites.origin: ALCE (Gao et al., 2023, arXiv:2305.14627): citation precision, i.e. does the cited passage support the statement
suites.adaptation: All verified facts re-checked deterministically against the stored source text (fresh normalization, independent of the stored verifier score); plus an LLM judge (gpt-5.4-mini) on a 50-fact systematic sample asking whether the source supports the summary, date and amount.

rows: Dr. Tsao's available records included the independent orthopedic examination report from Dr. Richard Semble dated September 13, 2023.

tables.title: Surfaced contradictions judged
rows: MRI interpretation disagrees on knee tears

The claims are genuinely inconsistent: one source reports objective MRI findings of horizontal tears in both knees, while another source interpreting the same MRIs says there was no recent traumatic injury or internal derangement. A meniscal tear is a form of internal derangement, so these are not merely different phrasings or compatible observations; they present a real dispute about what the MRIs showed.

The quoted statements are not a clear factual conflict. A "truck" can be a lay description of a Metro-North utility vehicle, so the doctor’s note is compatible with the intake/field-note descriptions rather than truly contradictory.

The claims present a real conflict: one source describes the 2023-08-08 MRI/DTI as abnormal and supportive of traumatic brain injury, while another says the same study shows no traumatic injury and is within normal limits. Those are directly incompatible interpretations of the same imaging, so this is a genuine contradiction worth flagging.

The cited descriptions are materially inconsistent about the crash mechanism: one version says the Metro-North vehicle merged into the client’s lane and struck him, while another says the client’s own vehicle struck the other vehicle as both merged. Those are not compatible ways of describing the same impact direction, so this is a real contradiction worth flagging.

The claims are genuinely inconsistent: the intake paperwork says the plaintiff denied prior work-related injuries and prior injury history, while the file also contains a 2011 left ankle/foot X-ray showing an avulsion fracture of the anterior talus. Those are not compatible facts, and the X-ray is direct evidence of a prior ankle injury that could contradict the denial.

The quoted statements are directly inconsistent on work capacity: the 2024 record says he was "totally disabled from his usual occupation," while the 2026 opinion says he is "able to work and perform activities of daily living without restrictions." A lawyer would likely treat this as a real impeachment issue because it reflects a materially different assessment of disability and employability.

These claims directly conflict: one source says the client "has not been discharged by anyone," while the emergency department record says the client was "Discharged home the same day" on 04/24/2023. A lawyer would likely view this as a real impeachment issue about discharge status and timing.

The cited items are not a clean contradiction. One note says the 22 scene photos had not yet been obtained; a later email says the sender had 22 photos on his phone and could send them, which is a compatible later update rather than a direct conflict. The separate document about plaintiff possessing 22 color-copied photos is also not necessarily the same thing as the scene photos referenced in the note.
Incident report was already in file

The claims directly conflict: one source says the Metro-North Railroad Incident Report was annexed to the discovery response, while a later email says the incident report had still not been produced and did not appear in the response. These are not compatible facts or a mere paraphrase, so this is a real contradiction.

The statements are not a real conflict. The first says coverage information would be provided separately, and the later email actually provides the bodily injury limits. That is a later update/fulfillment, not an inconsistent statement.
Police report said missing despite annexed copy

The claims are in real tension: one source says a copy of the Police Accident Report was annexed, while the later note says there is no police accident report in the file. A lawyer could view that as a genuine inconsistency about whether the report was present in the file/discovery materials, not merely a paraphrase or compatible detail.
Earlier note says no report obtained

The statements are not necessarily contradictory: the 2023-05-23 note says no police accident report had been obtained at that time, while the discovery response says a copy of the report was annexed, which could have happened later. Without proof the report was already available when the note was written, this is a chronological update rather than a real conflict.

suites.name: RAG quality (Ask the case)
suites.origin: RAGAS (Es et al., 2023, arXiv:2309.15217): faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision, context recall
suites.adaptation: 25 questions with gold answers and gold source refs written from the answer key. System = lib/server/retrieval/ask (query expansion + hybrid search k=15 + gpt-5.5 answer over verified facts and passages). One gpt-5.4-mini judge call per question produces the RAGAS intermediate judgments; answer relevancy = mean cosine (text-embedding-3-large) between the question and 3 judge-generated reverse questions, as in RAGAS. Contexts scored = top-10 retrieved passages. Caveat: ask also gives the answer model every verified fact line (not only the passages), but faithfulness here is judged against the top-10 passages only, so it is a lower bound.

suites.name: Retrieval ablation (hybrid vs vector vs keyword)
suites.origin: Standard IR recall@k (as in BEIR, Thakur et al., 2021, arXiv:2104.08663); RRF from Cormack et al., 2009
suites.adaptation: Same 25 questions, gold source refs from qa.json. Raw hybrid_search RPC (RRF k=60) with no query expansion and no dedup; vector-only passes an empty keyword query, keyword-only passes no embeddings. A doc page hit counts for its document. hit@k = any gold source in top k; recall@k = share of gold sources in top k.

suites.name: Long-document needle retrieval
suites.origin: Needle-in-a-Haystack (Kamradt, 2023) and RULER (Hsieh et al., 2024, arXiv:2404.06654); here on real pages, nothing planted
suites.adaptation: Longest document in the matter (04-medical-records__created__advanced-rockland-chiropractic-records-2023-04-26.pdf, 131 pages). Up to 4 pages per depth bucket chosen systematically; gpt-5.4-mini writes one question per page from a page-specific detail (questions committed in eval/results/suites/needle.questions.json). Retrieval = gist hybrid search (k=10, no expansion, with dedup). Page hit = the exact page in top 10; also reported straight from the hybrid_search RPC before the 2-per-document dedup cap. Caveat: daily treatment notes are repetitive, so near-duplicate pages make page-level hits harder and doc-level hits easier.

suites.name: Agent harness (Ask gist OS)
suites.origin: tau-bench (Yao et al., 2024, arXiv:2406.12045): programmatic task checks and the pass^k reliability metric
suites.adaptation: 10 tasks x 2 trials against lib/server/assistant/agent.ts with four programmatic checks (required tool, valid cites, gold key facts, no invented numbers). Implemented in scripts/eval.ts (suiteAgent).

Three attempts failed: two on the shared gpt-5.4-mini rate limit (200k TPM, shared with the live app and the other eval suites) and the third when the OpenAI organization ran out of API credits at 14:37 PT. suites.name: Per-profile memory
suites.origin: LongMemEval (Wu et al., 2024, arXiv:2410.10813): information extraction, knowledge update, temporal reasoning, abstention
suites.adaptation: Scripted multi-session run against the real assistant with a throwaway profile (all rows deleted after): 3 sessions state preferences/focus, 1 later session updates a preference, then 6 probe sessions. Each message is a new thread, so only profile_memories carries information across. An LLM judge (gpt-5.4-mini) grades each probe against the expected behavior.

suites.name: Cost and latency per case
suites.adaptation: The first true cold extraction was spread over several parallel development runs, so no single run is a clean cold run. We report: first_pass_extract_cost = earliest logged call per extraction shard (what a new case pays to extract); cold_run = the completed full pipeline run (extract + synth present) with the highest logged cost (its extraction was already cached; it paid for reconcile, gates, Jev and embeddings); warm run = latest completed full run whose extraction tasks were all cache hits. Costs are tokens x the hardcoded price table in lib/server/llm.ts (Jev cost is estimated from characters / 4). No fresh rerun was done for this eval to avoid mutating the live matter; timings are from logged runs.

suites.name: Single-shot long-context baseline
suites.origin: Long-context baseline in the style of RAG-vs-long-context comparisons (Li et al., 2024, arXiv:2407.16833)
suites.adaptation: One gpt-5.5 call (reasoning low) given the whole case text (all source items, then doc pages, cut at 900,000 chars) asked for a full digest plus answers to the 25 QA questions. Scored with the same recall judge and checklist as gist, and the same correctness judge as the RAG suite. One scored run (an earlier attempt died in judging after the model call; its prompt prefix was still in OpenAI's prompt cache, so the logged cost is mostly cached input; cost_usd_if_uncached is the list-price cost of the same tokens).
